options: A cloud-native SIEM and SOAR solution built directly on Microsoft Azure
An on-premises log server that must be sized and purchased in advance
A single antivirus product with no log correlation capability
A Linux-only open-source log aggregator unrelated to Azure
questions.explain: Sentinel combines SIEM (detection/correlation) and SOAR (automated response) in one cloud-native product built on Azure.

questions.q: What does 'cloud-native' change about Sentinel's cost and operations model, compared to a traditional on-prem SIEM?
options: No hardware to provision or maintain, and billing is based on actual data ingested/retained rather than pre-purchased capacity
It only changes where the physical servers are racked, nothing about cost
It requires buying even more hardware than an on-prem SIEM
It eliminates the need to ever ingest any log data
questions.explain: Sentinel runs on Azure's infrastructure, so there's no hardware to size or maintain, and cost scales with actual ingestion and retention.

questions.q: What does the 'SOAR' half of Sentinel add on top of the 'SIEM' half?
options: Automated response actions, like playbooks that can disable an account or open a ticket when an alert fires
A second, separate log storage system with no connection to alerts
A requirement that every alert be reviewed by two analysts before anything happens
Nothing — SOAR and SIEM are the same capability under different names
questions.explain: SOAR stands for Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response — it automates actions like playbooks in response to an alert the SIEM half generated.

questions.q: Why does bundling SIEM and SOAR into one product matter, according to this lesson?
options: It lets detection and automated response happen in one connected product instead of needing a separate SOAR tool bolted onto a SIEM
It makes the product only usable for detection, never for response
It has no practical benefit over using two unrelated tools
It means Sentinel cannot generate any alerts at all
questions.explain: Having both capabilities natively in one product, rather than stitching a separate SOAR tool onto a SIEM, is one of Sentinel's distinguishing design choices.

questions.q: Where do Sentinel and Microsoft Defender XDR increasingly live together today?
options: Inside a single, unified console — the Microsoft Defender portal
They cannot be used together under any circumstances
Only inside the classic Azure Portal, with no other option
Defender XDR replaced Sentinel entirely and Sentinel no longer exists
questions.explain: Microsoft has increasingly unified Sentinel with Defender XDR inside the Microsoft Defender portal, rather than keeping them as separate tools.
